# Ella IMS Documentation

> An IP Multimedia Subsystem for private 4G and 5G networks - easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

An IP Multimedia Subsystem for private 4G and 5G networks - easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

# Home

# Ella IMS

**Ella IMS** lets subscribers of a private 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. It is an IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) that runs as a single application, designed to be easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

## Key features

- **Voice and video calls** over 4G (VoLTE) and 5G (VoNR).
- **SIP trunks**: connect your private network to the public phone network.
- **SIM-based authentication** with your existing HSS (IMS-AKA over Cx), and IPsec between phones and the IMS.
- **Voice QoS** from the 4G or 5G core: PCRF over Rx, or PCF over N5 with optional mutual TLS.
- **Application Servers**: connect voicemail, conferencing, supplementary services and other services, routed per subscriber by your HSS (iFCs over ISC).
- **Push-to-talk**: a built-in MCPTT server for group calls with floor control, and an Android client.
- **Call records**: who called whom, when, for how long, and how the call ended.
- **Easy to operate**: a single binary with an embedded database, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics.

# Tutorials

# Tutorials

These tutorials walk you through Ella IMS, from your first voice call to running it on Kubernetes.

| Tutorial                                                                                                                     | Hardware Required                                        | Installation Method | Duration |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------- |
| [Make Your First Voice Call](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/tutorials/first_voice_call/index.md)                          | An Ella Core 5G network, a second Linux host, two phones | Snap                | ~30 min  |
| [Run a High Availability Cluster in the Cloud](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/tutorials/ha_cluster_in_the_cloud/index.md) | None, a Google Cloud project or an AWS account           | Kubernetes          | ~45 min  |

# Make Your First Voice Call

In this tutorial, we will add Ella IMS to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and make a voice call (VoNR) between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

## Pre-requisites

To complete this tutorial, you will need the following:

**Ella Core**

- A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's [Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware)](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/tutorials/getting_started_hardware/) tutorial. In this tutorial, Ella Core's N6 interface, `ens3`, has the address `10.6.0.2`.

**Ella IMS**

- A second Linux machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, on Ella Core's N6 network. In this tutorial, it has the address `10.6.0.5`.

**Phones**

- Two [5G phones that support VoNR](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/supported_mobile_equipment/#phones), each with a SIM provisioned as a subscriber in Ella Core.

## 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core

On the Ella Core machine, edit the configuration file:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
```

Under `interfaces`, add the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

```
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.6.0.2"
```

Restart Ella Core:

```
sudo snap restart ella-core.cored
```

## 2. Install Ella IMS

On the Ella IMS machine, install the Ella IMS snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control
```

Edit the configuration file:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
```

Set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from:

/var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

```
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.6.0.5
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd
```

## 3. Initialize Ella IMS

Open your browser and navigate to `http://10.6.0.5:5020/`. The **Initialize Ella IMS** page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click **Create**. You should see Ella IMS's **Cores** page.

## 4. Connect Ella IMS to Ella Core

Go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **Peers**, click **Add Peer**, enter `10.6.0.2`, check **HSS** and **PCRF**, and click **Add**.
- Under **HSS**, click the edit icon next to **HSS Realm**, enter `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.
- Under **Voice QoS**, click the edit icon next to **Policy Function**, select **PCRF**, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **PCRF Realm**, enter `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.

Under **Peers**, Ella Core should show as **open**.

## 5. Route the phones' traffic

On the Ella IMS machine, route the phones' voice addresses, which we create in the next step, through Ella Core:

```
sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400
```

## 6. Prepare Ella Core for voice

In the Ella Core UI, go to the **Operator** page and scroll to the **IMS** section. Click the edit icon next to **P-CSCF Addresses**, enter `10.6.0.5`, and click **Update**.

Go to the **Networking** page and open the **Data Networks** tab. Click **Create**, enter `ims` as the **Name**, `10.46.0.0/16` as the **IPv4 Pool**, turn on **IMS (voice and mission critical services)**, and click **Create**.

Go to the **Profiles** page and click on the `default` profile. Click **Add Policy**, enter `voice` as the **Name**, set the **Data Network** to `ims`, and click **Create**.

Go to the **Subscribers** page. For each of the two subscribers, click on it, click the edit icon next to **MSISDN**, enter a number, and click **Update**:

- First subscriber: `+15551230001`
- Second subscriber: `+15551230002`

## 7. Register the phones

On each phone, turn on VoNR, then turn airplane mode on and off.

In Ella IMS, go to the **Registrations** page. You should see both phones.

## 8. Make a call

From the first phone, call `+15551230002`. Answer on the second phone, talk, and hang up.

In Ella IMS, go to the **Calls** page. You should see the call, with the outcome **answered**.

Success

Congratulations! You have made a voice call over your private 5G network, through Ella Core and Ella IMS.

# Run a High Availability Cluster in the Cloud

In this tutorial, you run Ella IMS as a three-node cluster on managed Kubernetes, and watch it survive the loss of a node and a rolling restart.

Note

This tutorial uses managed Kubernetes. Ella IMS can also run as a cluster on cloud virtual machines, installed as a snap, as in [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md).

## Pre-requisites

- A Google Cloud project and the `gcloud` CLI with the `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin` component

- `kubectl` and `git`.

- An AWS account and the `aws` CLI

- `eksctl`, `kubectl` and `git`.

## 1. Create a Kubernetes cluster

```
gcloud container clusters create ella-ims \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type e2-standard-2 \
  --num-nodes 1 \
  --enable-dataplane-v2 \
  --enable-ip-alias \
  --enable-multi-networking
gcloud container clusters get-credentials ella-ims --zone us-central1-a
```

Create `cluster.yaml`:

```
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
metadata:
  name: ella-ims
  region: us-east-1
availabilityZones: [us-east-1a, us-east-1b]
addons:
  - name: vpc-cni
    configurationValues: '{"enableNetworkPolicy":"true"}'
  - name: eks-pod-identity-agent
  - name: aws-ebs-csi-driver
    useDefaultPodIdentityAssociations: true
    configurationValues: '{"defaultStorageClass":{"enabled":true}}'
managedNodeGroups:
  - name: ella-ims
    instanceType: t3.medium
    desiredCapacity: 3
    availabilityZones: [us-east-1a]
```

Create the cluster:

```
eksctl create cluster -f cluster.yaml
```

## 2. Create the SIP network

```
gcloud compute networks create ims-sip --subnet-mode custom
gcloud compute networks subnets create ims-sip \
  --network ims-sip \
  --region us-central1 \
  --range 10.60.0.0/24
gcloud compute firewall-rules create ims-sip-allow-internal \
  --network ims-sip \
  --allow esp,udp,tcp,icmp \
  --source-ranges 10.60.0.0/24
```

```
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
VPC=$(aws eks describe-cluster --name ella-ims --query cluster.resourcesVpcConfig.vpcId --output text)
SUBNET=$(aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $VPC \
  --availability-zone us-east-1a \
  --cidr-block 192.168.128.0/24 \
  --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=ims-sip}]' \
  --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text)
SG=$(aws ec2 create-security-group --vpc-id $VPC \
  --group-name ims-sip \
  --description "Ella IMS SIP" \
  --query GroupId --output text)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $SG --protocol all --cidr 192.168.128.0/24
```

## 3. Connect the nodes to the SIP network

Create three nodes with a second NIC on the SIP subnet. Each Ella IMS node runs on one of them, with that NIC as `eth1`:

```
gcloud container node-pools create ims-sip \
  --cluster ella-ims \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type e2-standard-2 \
  --num-nodes 3 \
  --image-type UBUNTU_CONTAINERD \
  --additional-node-network network=ims-sip,subnetwork=ims-sip
```

Give each node a second NIC on the SIP subnet. Each Ella IMS node runs on one of them, with that NIC as `eth1`:

```
for i in $(aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --filters Name=tag:eks:cluster-name,Values=ella-ims Name=instance-state-name,Values=running \
  --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' --output text); do
  ENI=$(aws ec2 create-network-interface --subnet-id $SUBNET --groups $SG \
    --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=network-interface,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=ims-sip},{Key=node.k8s.amazonaws.com/no_manage,Value=true}]' \
    --query NetworkInterface.NetworkInterfaceId --output text)
  aws ec2 attach-network-interface --network-interface-id $ENI --instance-id $i --device-index 2
done
```

Install Multus, which gives the NIC to the pod:

```
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni/v4.3.1/deployments/multus-daemonset-thick.yml
kubectl rollout status daemonset/kube-multus-ds -n kube-system
```

## 4. Deploy Ella IMS

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
kubectl create secret generic ella-ims-cluster -n ella --from-literal=secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/examples/gke-ha
kubectl get pods -n ella --watch
```

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
kubectl create secret generic ella-ims-cluster -n ella --from-literal=secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/examples/eks-ha
kubectl get pods -n ella --watch
```

Wait until the three pods are `Running`, then press `Ctrl+C`.

## 5. Initialize Ella IMS

```
kubectl port-forward -n ella pod/ella-ims-0 5020:5020
```

Open `http://localhost:5020` and create the first user.

## 6. Look at the cluster

Open the **Cluster** page. It names the leader. Only the leader shows the health of the nodes: if `ella-ims-0` is not the leader, stop the port-forward with `Ctrl+C`, and start it again on the leader's pod:

```
kubectl port-forward -n ella pod/ella-ims-<n> 5020:5020
```

On the leader's **Cluster** page, the three nodes appear as **Healthy**, each with its own **Diameter Host**.

## 7. Lose a node

In another terminal, delete the leader's pod:

```
kubectl delete pod -n ella ella-ims-<n>
```

The port-forward stops with the pod. Start it again on another pod, and open the **Cluster** page: another node is the leader. Open the new leader's page as in step 6. The deleted pod comes back, and its node returns to **Healthy** with the same **Diameter Host**.

## 8. Restart the nodes one at a time

Stop the port-forward, then:

```
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/ella-ims -n ella
kubectl rollout status statefulset/ella-ims -n ella
```

Open the leader's **Cluster** page as in step 6: all three nodes are **Healthy**.

## 9. Clean up

```
kubectl delete statefulset ella-ims -n ella --wait
kubectl wait --for=delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ella-ims -n ella --timeout=2m
kubectl delete -k ims/k8s/examples/gke-ha --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete pvc -n ella --all
kubectl wait --for=delete pv --all --timeout=5m
gcloud container clusters delete ella-ims --zone us-central1-a
gcloud compute firewall-rules delete ims-sip-allow-internal
gcloud compute networks subnets delete ims-sip --region us-central1
gcloud compute networks delete ims-sip
```

```
kubectl delete statefulset ella-ims -n ella --wait
kubectl wait --for=delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ella-ims -n ella --timeout=2m
kubectl delete -k ims/k8s/examples/eks-ha --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete pvc -n ella --all
kubectl wait --for=delete pv --all --timeout=5m
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
for ENI in $(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=ims-sip \
  --query 'NetworkInterfaces[].NetworkInterfaceId' --output text); do
  aws ec2 detach-network-interface --attachment-id $(aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces \
    --network-interface-ids $ENI --query 'NetworkInterfaces[0].Attachment.AttachmentId' --output text)
  aws ec2 wait network-interface-available --network-interface-ids $ENI
  aws ec2 delete-network-interface --network-interface-id $ENI
done
aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id $(aws ec2 describe-security-groups \
  --filters Name=group-name,Values=ims-sip --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' --output text)
aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $(aws ec2 describe-subnets \
  --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=ims-sip --query 'Subnets[0].SubnetId' --output text)
eksctl delete cluster -f cluster.yaml --wait
```

# Back Up and Restore

Store and transfer backups encrypted.

## Back up

1. Create an API token for an admin: in **Users**, open the user, and in **API Tokens**, click **Create Token**.

1. Download a backup:

   ```
   curl -fOJ http://<host-ip>:5020/api/v1/backup \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ellaims_..."
   ```

   This saves `ims-backup-<time>.tar.gz`. In a cluster, back up from any node.

1. Create an API token for an admin: in **Users**, open the user, and in **API Tokens**, click **Create Token**.

1. Open the API:

   ```
   kubectl port-forward -n ella svc/ella-ims 5020:5020
   ```

1. Download a backup:

   ```
   curl -fOJ http://localhost:5020/api/v1/backup \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ellaims_..."
   ```

   This saves `ims-backup-<time>.tar.gz`.

## Restore

1. Log in as an admin, and keep the token:

   ```
   TOKEN=$(curl -s http://<host-ip>:5020/api/v1/auth/login \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"email": "admin@example.com", "password": "..."}' | jq -r .result.token)
   ```

1. Restore the backup:

   ```
   curl http://<host-ip>:5020/api/v1/restore \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \
     --data-binary @ims-backup-<time>.tar.gz
   ```

   In a cluster, restore on the leader. Another node answers `421` with the leader's address.

1. Open the API of the leader's pod, named on the **Cluster** page, or `ella-ims-0` for a standalone node:

   ```
   kubectl port-forward -n ella pod/ella-ims-<n> 5020:5020
   ```

1. Log in as an admin, and keep the token:

   ```
   TOKEN=$(curl -s http://localhost:5020/api/v1/auth/login \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"email": "admin@example.com", "password": "..."}' | jq -r .result.token)
   ```

1. Restore the backup:

   ```
   curl http://localhost:5020/api/v1/restore \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \
     --data-binary @ims-backup-<time>.tar.gz
   ```

## Disaster recovery

Use this procedure when a cluster lost a majority of its nodes, or a standalone node was lost.

1. Install Ella IMS on a new host, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md). For a cluster, add a `cluster` block to the configuration file.

1. Open `http://<host-ip>:5020` in a browser and initialize it with a temporary user.

1. Restore the backup with that user, as in [Restore](#restore).

1. For a standalone deployment, stop here.

1. Log in with a user from the backup, and add the other nodes, as in [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md), steps 2 to 4. Delete the data of any node that was in the old cluster first:

   ```
   sudo snap stop ella-ims.imsd
   sudo rm -rf /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.db* /var/snap/ella-ims/common/node.db* /var/snap/ella-ims/common/raft
   sudo snap start ella-ims.imsd
   ```

1. Delete the cluster and its volumes:

   ```
   kubectl delete -k ims/k8s/ha
   kubectl delete pvc -n ella -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ella-ims
   ```

1. Deploy it again:

   ```
   kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/ha
   ```

1. Initialize it with a temporary user, as in [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md), step 2.

1. Restore the backup with that user, as in [Restore](#restore).

# Configure Single Sign-On

This guide lets users sign in to the Ella IMS UI through an OpenID Connect identity provider. It gives the steps for Keycloak; other providers are set up the same way.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella IMS**: served over HTTPS, at a URL with no path.
- **Identity provider**: an OpenID Connect provider, reachable from Ella IMS over HTTPS.
- **Ella IMS account**: an Admin that signs in with a password.

The examples use these values:

| Value                                               | Role                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `https://ims.example.com`                           | Ella IMS's external URL                                                 |
| `https://ims.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback` | Redirect URL: the external URL followed by `/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback` |

## 1. Register Ella IMS at the identity provider

In the realm users sign in to:

1. Go to **Clients** and click **Create client**.
1. Set **Client type** to **OpenID Connect** and **Client ID** to `ims`. Click **Next**.
1. Turn on **Client authentication**. Keep **Standard flow** checked. Click **Next**.
1. Set **Valid redirect URIs** to the redirect URL. Click **Save**.
1. In the client's **Credentials** tab, copy the **Client Secret**.

In **Users**, turn on **Email verified** for each user.

1. Register a web application, or confidential client, with the redirect URL.
1. Create a client secret for it.
1. Allow the `openid`, `email` and `profile` scopes.

If the provider does not send `email_verified`, turn on **Trust email addresses from this provider** in step 2.

## 2. Configure Ella IMS

In the UI, go to **Single Sign-On** and, in **Provider**, click **Edit**. Set:

| Field                                        | Value                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **External URL**                             | `https://ims.example.com`                                                                   |
| **Issuer URL**                               | Keycloak: `https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm>`. Otherwise, from the provider.           |
| **CA certificate**                           | The PEM CA certificate of the identity provider, only if a private CA signs its certificate |
| **Client ID**                                | Keycloak: `ims`. Otherwise, from the provider.                                              |
| **Client secret**                            | The secret from step 1                                                                      |
| **Display name**                             | The name on the login button, such as `Keycloak`                                            |
| **Scopes**                                   | `openid email profile`                                                                      |
| **Session lifetime**                         | `24` hours, or less to end access sooner after offboarding                                  |
| **Trust email addresses from this provider** | Off, unless the provider does not send `email_verified`                                     |

Check that the **Redirect URL** under the external URL is the one registered in step 1.

## 3. Test the identity provider

In the dialog, click **Test**. Fix the issuer URL or the CA certificate until it shows **Works**. Click **Update**.

## 4. Enable single sign-on

On the **Single Sign-On** page, click **Enable**.

To turn it off, for example during an incident, click **Disable**. Everyone who logged in with single sign-on is signed out.

## 5. Sign in

1. Give a user access: [create their user](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#give-a-user-access), or [map their groups to a role](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#map-groups-to-roles).
1. In a private browser window, open `https://ims.example.com`, and click **Log in with** your display name.
1. Sign in at the identity provider. Ella IMS opens.

If the login page shows an error, the `auth_oidc_login` [audit event](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/observability/#audit-events) in the logs gives the reason.

# Connect a Core at Another Site

This guide connects Ella IMS, on Kubernetes or elsewhere, to a core, such as Ella Core, at another site.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella IMS**: installed and started, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md).
- **For SMS over IP**: the HSS, and the MME or SMSF, support SCTP for Diameter.

The examples use these addresses:

| Address        | Role                                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `10.6.0.5`     | Ella IMS's P-CSCF address                                    |
| `10.4.0.12`    | Ella IMS's Diameter address, the pod's address on Kubernetes |
| `10.3.0.2`     | Diameter address of the core's HSS and PCRF                  |
| `10.46.0.0/16` | IP pool of the core's `ims` data network                     |

## 1. Link the two sites

Set up a routed link, such as an IPsec VPN like [Google Cloud VPN](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview), between the core's site and the network of `10.6.0.5`. Keep NAT out of the path from the core's N6 or SGi interface to `10.6.0.5`.

Use address ranges that don't overlap between the two sites, nor with any other site on the same VPN. On Ella IMS's side, this includes the node subnets, the pod range and the subnet of `10.6.0.5`.

## 2. Route the phones' traffic

- At the core's site, route `10.6.0.5` from the core's N6 or SGi interface through the link.
- On Ella IMS's side, route `10.46.0.0/16` through the link.

## 3. Allow SIP and ESP

From `10.46.0.0/16` to `10.6.0.5`, allow:

- UDP and TCP port `5060`.
- ESP, carrying UDP and TCP ports `5063`, `5064` and `5065`.

## 4. Route and allow Diameter

- At the core's site, route `10.4.0.12` through the link.
- On Ella IMS's side, route `10.3.0.2` through the link.
- Allow TCP or SCTP port `3868` from `10.4.0.12` to `10.3.0.2`. For SMS over IP, allow SCTP.

## 5. Point the core and Ella IMS at each other

- In the core, set the P-CSCF address to `10.6.0.5`. In Ella Core, it is **Operator → IMS → P-CSCF Addresses**.
- In Ella IMS, go to the **Cores** page. Under **Peers**, click **Create Peer**, enter `10.3.0.2`, check **HSS**, **PCRF** and **Sh**, and click **Create**. For SMS over IP, also check **S6c**, and set **Transport** to **SCTP**.
- Set the realms, as in [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/index.md), step 2.

## 6. Verify

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Cores** page. Under **Peers**, the core shows **open**.

Register a phone and make a call.

# Connect to a SIP Trunk

This guide connects Ella IMS to a carrier's SIP trunk, for calls to and from numbers outside the HSS. The example carrier is [Telnyx](https://telnyx.com), any other carrier should work similarly.

The examples use these addresses:

| Address                                          | Role                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `203.0.113.5`                                    | Ella IMS's address towards the carrier |
| `sip.telnyx.com`                                 | Telnyx's SIP domain                    |
| `192.76.120.10`, `64.16.250.10`, `192.76.120.14` | Addresses Telnyx sends calls from      |

## Prerequisites

- **Ella IMS**: connected to the core network, as in [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/index.md) or [Integrate with Open5GS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_open5gs/index.md), with the **Numbering Plan** set on the **Operator** page.
- **SIP trunk**: an IP-authenticated trunk.
- **Numbers**: the carrier's numbers, set as the subscribers' MSISDNs in the HSS.

## 1. Enable the IBCF

In `ims.yaml`, set the address carriers reach Ella IMS on, and restart Ella IMS:

```
ibcf:
  external:
    addresses:
      - address: 203.0.113.5
```

In a cluster, set each node's own address on that node.

## 2. Open the firewall

Allow SIP (TCP `5060`) from Telnyx's addresses, and voice (UDP `10000`–`19999`) from [Telnyx's media networks](https://sip.telnyx.com), to `203.0.113.5`. In a cluster, do the same for each node's address.

## 3. Configure the carrier

In the carrier portal, create an IP connection:

- Send calls to `203.0.113.5`, port `5060`, over TCP. In a cluster, add each node's address, or a host name that resolves to all of them.
- Enable AMR-WB.
- Send called numbers in E.164 format, with `+`.
- Attach an outbound voice profile.
- Assign your numbers to the connection.

## 4. Add the trunk

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **SIP Trunks** page and click **Create Trunk**:

- **Name**: `Telnyx`.
- **Host**: `sip.telnyx.com`.
- **Inbound CIDRs**: `192.76.120.10/32`, `64.16.250.10/32` and `192.76.120.14/32`, one per line.
- Check **Trusted**.

Click **Create**.

## 5. Add a route

On the **SIP Trunks** page, click **Create Route**. Leave **Prefix** empty, select `Telnyx` under **Add Trunk**, and click **Create**.

## 6. Check the trunk is up

On the **SIP Trunks** page, the trunk's **State** should be `up` within a minute.

## 7. Place a test call

From a registered phone, call an outside number in international format, e.g. `+15555550100`. Then call one of your numbers from an outside phone.

Both calls should have audio both ways.

# Deploy a High Availability Cluster

Ella IMS can be deployed as a high-availability cluster to provide redundancy and failover capabilities. See [High Availability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/high_availability/index.md) for more information.

## Prerequisites

- Three hosts meeting the standard [system requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/system_reqs/index.md).
- Ella IMS installed on each host via the [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md) guide, with `cluster.address` set in the configuration file.
- An HSS that supports IMS restoration.

## 1. Start node 1

Start node 1, open a browser at the API address and initialize it normally.

## 2. Create a join token for node 2

Still in node 1, open the **Cluster** page, click **Add Node**, click **Create Token**, then copy the token.

## 3. Start node 2

Start node 2, open a browser at the API address and click **Join an existing cluster instead**. Paste the token and click **Join**.

## 4. Add node 3

Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node 3.

## 5. Connect the network

- On the HSS and the PCRF, accept every node's Diameter host, shown on the **Cluster** page.
- In the core network, set the P-CSCF addresses to every node's SIP address.
- On each carrier, add every node's IBCF address.

## 6. Verify

On the leader's **Cluster** page, all three nodes appear as **Healthy**.

## Prerequisites

- A Kubernetes cluster with three nodes meeting the [system requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/system_reqs/index.md).
- A second interface, `eth1`, for each pod, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md).
- An HSS that supports IMS restoration.

## 1. Deploy

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
kubectl create secret generic ella-ims-cluster -n ella --from-literal=secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/ha
```

## 2. Initialize

```
kubectl port-forward -n ella pod/ella-ims-0 5020:5020
```

Open `http://localhost:5020` and initialize it normally.

## 3. Connect the network

- On the HSS and the PCRF, accept every pod's Diameter host, shown on the **Cluster** page.
- In the core network, set the P-CSCF addresses to every pod's SIP address.

## 4. Verify

On the leader's **Cluster** page, all three nodes appear as **Healthy**.

# Enable Push-to-Talk

This guide enables group calls with floor control with Ella IMS's built-in Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) server. The examples use `10.6.0.5` as Ella IMS's SIP address.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella Core**: integrated with Ella IMS, as in [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/index.md), and serving as the HSS.
- **Phones**: the Ella MCPTT app, installed as in [Install the Android MCPTT App](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install_android_app/index.md), and a native IMS client that registers with a `reg-id`.
- **SIMs**: with an ISIM you can program.

## 1. Enable the MCPTT server

In `ims.yaml`, set the address phones reach the MCPTT media on, and restart Ella IMS:

```
mcptt:
  media:
    address: 10.6.0.5
```

## 2. Configure Ella Core

In the Ella Core UI:

- **Networking → Data Networks → Create**: `mcx`, with an IP pool and **IMS** on.
- **Profiles → Create**: an MC profile, e.g. `mcptt`. On it, **Add Policy**: a name, data network `mcx`, 5QI/QCI `69`, ARP `3`, **May pre-empt**, **Not pre-emptable**.
- On the MC profile, also add the policies the users had on their previous profile, e.g. `internet` and `ims`.
- **Operator → IMS → Add Application Server**: click **Fill for Ella IMS MCPTT**, then **Add**.
- **Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile**: name `mcptt`; under **Add from preset**, select the **MCPTT** preset and click **Add Criteria**, then click **Add**.
- **Profiles →** the MC profile **→** edit **IMS Service Profiles**: set **MCPTT** to `mcptt`, and **MMTel (voice, SMS)** to the service profile of the users' previous profile, if any, then **Save**.
- **Subscribers**: put each user on the MC profile, with an MSISDN.

## 3. Route the MC traffic

On the Ella IMS host, route the `mcx` IP pool through Ella Core's N6 address, e.g.:

```
sudo ip route add 10.47.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400
```

## 4. Add the users

In the Ella IMS UI, go to **Push-to-Talk → Users**. For each person, click **Add User** and enter:

- **MCPTT ID**: e.g. `alice`.
- **IMS Identities**: the subscriber's MSISDN, e.g. `15550000001`.

## 5. Add a group

Go to **Push-to-Talk → Groups**, click **Add Group**, and enter a group ID, e.g. `fire`, and its members.

## 6. Set up the phones

On each phone:

- Program the SIM's ISIM with `sip:mcptt-<MSISDN>@<home domain>` in a record of EF.IMPU after the first.
- Set the APN to `mcx`.
- In the app's settings, set the user's MCPTT ID as Ella IMS shows it, e.g. `alice@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and groups.

## 7. Make a group call

Start a group call from one phone. The other members' phones should ring, and **Push-to-Talk → Calls** should show the call.

A group call in the Ella MCPTT app

# Enable SMS over IP

This guide lets phones send and receive SMS over IMS with Ella IMS's built-in IP-SM-GW. The examples use `10.3.0.7` as the SMSC's Diameter address and `15550000000` as its service centre address.

## Prerequisites

- **HSS**: an HSS connected to Ella IMS that supports the Sh-Update of SMSRegistrationInfo and forwards routing requests to the IP-SM-GW over S6c.
- **SMSC**: an SMSC with an SGd interface, such as Ella SMSC.
- **MME or SMSF**, for delivery over NAS when IMS fails: reachable over SGd.

## 1. Set the IP-SM-GW number

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **SMS over IP** page. Under **IP-SM-GW**, click the edit icon next to **Number**, enter an E.164 number without `+`, e.g. `15550000100`, and click **Update**.

## 2. Add the SMSC peer

Go to the **Cores** page. Under **Peers**, click **Create Peer**, and enter:

- **Address**: `10.3.0.7`, or the SMSC's host name, e.g. `smsc-0.smsc.ella.svc.cluster.local`.
- **Host**: the SMSC's Diameter identity, e.g. `smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org` for Ella SMSC.
- **Roles**: **SGd** only.
- **Transport**: **SCTP**, for Ella SMSC.

Click **Create**. For an Ella SMSC cluster, create a peer for each node, with the node's address and host.

## 3. Let the HSS reach the IP-SM-GW

On the **Cores** page, edit the HSS peer, check **Sh** and **S6c**, and click **Update**. If the HSS's core also serves the MME or SMSF, check **SGd** too, for fallback to SMS over NAS.

## 4. Route the service centre to the SMSC

Go to the **SMS over IP** page. Under **Routes**, click **Create Route**, and enter:

- **Service Centre**: `15550000000`, or leave empty for the default route.
- **SMSC Peers**: check the SMSC peers.

Click **Create**.

## 5. Add iFCs in the HSS

With Ella Core:

- **Operator → IMS → Add Application Server**: name `ip-sm-gw`, the **Name** of the **IP-SM-GW** on the **SMS over IP** page as the **Server Name**, then **Add**.
- **Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile**: name `sms-over-ip`; under **Add from preset**, select the **SMS over IP** preset and the `ip-sm-gw` **Application Server**, click **Add Criteria**, then click **Add**.
- **Profiles →** the subscribers' profile **→** edit **IMS Service Profiles**: set **MMTel (voice, SMS)** to `sms-over-ip`, then **Save**.

With another HSS, add two iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the **Name** of the **IP-SM-GW** on the **SMS over IP** page as the server name, e.g. `sip:ipsmgw.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and default handling `SESSION_CONTINUED`:

- A trigger point on method `REGISTER`, with the subscriber's MSISDN as the service information, and **Include Register Request** and **Include Register Response** set.
- A trigger point on method `MESSAGE`, session case `ORIGINATING_REGISTERED`, and header `Content-Type` matching `application/vnd\.3gpp\.sms`.

## 6. Verify

Register a phone with SMS over IP enabled, and send an SMS. `ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total` should count it, with direction `mo` and result `success`.

# Install

Choose one of the installation methods below.

Install the Ella IMS snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control
```

Configure Ella IMS:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd
```

Ella IMS's UI and API are at `http://<host-ip>:5020`.

Install the required dependencies:

```
sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc
```

Clone the Ella IMS repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
cd ims
```

Build the frontend:

```
npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui
```

Build Ella IMS:

```
go build -o ims -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/ims/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/ims
```

Configure Ella IMS:

```
vim ims.yaml
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo ./ims --config ims.yaml
```

Ella IMS's UI and API are at `http://<host-ip>:5020`.

Create a new directory:

```
mkdir ella-ims
cd ella-ims
```

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml

```
configs:
  ella_ims_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/ims.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5020
      sip:
        addresses: [10.6.0.5]
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.5

services:
  ella-ims:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-ims:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_ims_config
        target: /ims.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/ims --config /ims.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    stop_grace_period: 37s
    network_mode: host
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    volumes:
      - ella-ims-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-ims-data:
```

Set `sip.addresses` and `diameter.address` to addresses of the host.

Start the Ella IMS container:

```
docker compose up -d
```

Ella IMS's UI and API are at `http://<host-ip>:5020`.

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster nodes meet the [system requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/system_reqs/index.md).

Download the Ella IMS manifests:

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
```

Create the namespace with the privileged Pod Security Standard:

```
kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged
```

Choose an example:

| Example                          | Second interface, `eth1`                                                                                                                                          | Files to edit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ims/k8s/examples/multus`        | [Multus](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni), with the `macvlan` and `static` CNI plugins on the nodes                                            | `ims-sip-nad.yaml`: set `master` to the node's interface on the network phones reach Ella IMS on, the P-CSCF address, and the route to the phones' IP pool through the core's N6 (5G) or SGi (4G) address.                                                                                     |
| `ims/k8s/examples/gke-netdevice` | [GKE multi-network](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/setup-multinetwork-support-for-pods) and an internal passthrough Network Load Balancer | `ims-sip-network.yaml`: set `vpc`, `vpcSubnet`, and the phones' IP pool in `routes`. Keep the routes for Google Cloud's health check ranges. `ims.yaml`: set `sip.addresses` to the load balancer's address. `kustomization.yaml`: set the same address in the `pcscf-address` init container. |

Give the pod its second interface, `eth1`, on the network phones reach Ella IMS on, as the example requires.

Edit the example's addresses in its files.

Deploy Ella IMS:

```
kubectl apply -k ims/k8s/examples/<example>
```

Find the P-CSCF address, the `pcscf` entry of `sip`:

```
kubectl logs -n ella ella-ims-0 | grep '"ims started"'
```

Open the UI and API on your machine:

```
kubectl port-forward -n ella svc/ella-ims 5020:5020
```

Ella IMS's UI and API are at `http://localhost:5020`.

On the HSS and the PCRF, set Ella IMS's Diameter host to `ella-ims-0.ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`, and accept its connections from the pod's address, or from the node's where the cluster masquerades pod traffic.

Open the UI and create the first user.

See the [configuration reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md) for all options.

# Install the Android MCPTT App

This guide installs Ella MCPTT, the push-to-talk app for Ella IMS, on Android phones.

## Prerequisites

- **Phones**: Android 14 or later.
- **SIMs**: access rules (ARA-M) that allow the app's signing certificate, SHA-1 `692EDA27666062D3982DF420E1FEC26FE806335B`.

## 1. Download the app

Download the app and its checksum, and check them:

```
curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk
curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk.sha256
sha256sum -c ella-mcptt.apk.sha256
```

## 2. Install the app

In your MDM, add `ella-mcptt.apk` as a private or in-house app, and assign it to the phones.

Connect the phone over USB, with USB debugging on, and run:

```
adb install -r ella-mcptt.apk
```

In the phone's browser, open `https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk`, allow the browser to install unknown apps, and install it.

## 3. Grant the permissions

Open Ella MCPTT and go to **Settings → Diagnostics → Permissions**. Tap **Allow** on each item, and allow it in the prompt. It should show **The app has everything it needs.**

To update the app, install a newer APK the same way. Its settings are kept.

# Integrate with an Application Server

This guide connects an Application Server (AS), such as voicemail or conferencing, to Ella IMS. The examples use `10.80.0.30` as the AS's address and `10.6.0.5` as Ella IMS's SIP address.

## Prerequisites

- **HSS**: an HSS that provisions initial Filter Criteria (iFCs).

## 1. Trust the AS

In `ims.yaml`, add the AS's address to the trusted networks, optionally set how long the AS has to answer, and restart Ella IMS:

```
sip:
  trusted_networks: [10.80.0.30/32]
scscf:
  as_timeout: 4s
```

## 2. Add iFCs in the HSS

In the HSS, add iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the AS's SIP URI as the server name, e.g. `sip:10.80.0.30:5060`:

- For third-party registration, add a trigger point on method `REGISTER`. Set **Include Register Request** and **Include Register Response** if the AS needs them.
- For originating or terminating services, add a trigger point on the session case, plus the method, header or Request-URI to match.
- Set the default handling to `SESSION_CONTINUED` to go on without the AS, or to `SESSION_TERMINATED` to fail the call, or deregister the user on `REGISTER`.

## 3. Add the AS's PSIs

If the AS serves its own URIs, such as a conference factory:

- Add its PSIs to the HSS, distinct or wildcarded, with their iFCs or the AS as their server name.
- If the server name is a host name, make it resolve to the AS, with a DNS A or SRV record.

## 4. Configure the AS

On the AS:

- Trust Ella IMS's SIP address, `10.6.0.5`.
- Send requests to a user to the I-CSCF, port `5070`.
- Send requests on behalf of a user or a PSI to the S-CSCF, port `5080`, with `orig` in the Route header, `Route: <sip:10.6.0.5:5080;lr;orig>`, and the user in P-Served-User or P-Asserted-Identity.

## 5. Verify

Register a phone. The AS should receive a third-party REGISTER, or the first request that matches its iFCs.

# Integrate with Ella Core

This guide connects Ella IMS to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS and the PCRF.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella IMS**: installed and started, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md).
- **Ella Core**: installed and started, as in its [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/install/) guide.

The examples use these addresses:

| Address        | Role                                      |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `10.3.0.2`     | Ella Core's Diameter address              |
| `10.6.0.2`     | Ella Core's N6 address                    |
| `10.3.0.5`     | Ella IMS's Diameter address               |
| `10.6.0.5`     | Ella IMS's SIP address                    |
| `10.46.0.0/16` | IP pool of Ella Core's `ims` data network |

## 1. Set the Ella IMS addresses

In `ims.yaml`, set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from, and restart Ella IMS:

```
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.5
```

## 2. Add Ella Core as the HSS and PCRF

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **Peers**, click **Create Peer**, enter `10.3.0.2`, check **HSS** and **PCRF**, and click **Create**.
- Under **HSS**, click the edit icon next to **HSS Realm**, enter `epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`, with the MNC padded to 3 digits, e.g. `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.
- Under **Voice QoS**, click the edit icon next to **Policy Function**, select **PCRF**, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **PCRF Realm**, enter the same realm, and click **Update**.

## 3. Route the phones' traffic

On the Ella IMS host, route the `ims` data network through Ella Core's N6 address:

```
sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400
```

## 4. Configure Ella Core

In Ella Core's configuration file, set the Diameter address, and restart Ella Core:

```
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"
```

In Ella Core, set **Operator → IMS → P-CSCF Addresses** to `10.6.0.5`, then follow Ella Core's [Enable Voice](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/enable_voice/) guide.

# Integrate with Open5GS

This guide connects Ella IMS to an Open5GS 5G core, with Open5GS as the HSS and the PCF.

## Prerequisites

- **Ella IMS**: installed and started, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md).
- **Open5GS**: a 5G core set up as in its [Quickstart](https://open5gs.org/open5gs/docs/guide/01-quickstart/), built from `main` or a release after v2.8.0.

The examples use these addresses:

| Address        | Role                           |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `10.0.0.10`    | Open5GS's address              |
| `10.0.0.20`    | Ella IMS's address             |
| `10.45.0.0/16` | IP pool of Open5GS's `ims` DNN |

## 1. Set the Ella IMS addresses

In `ims.yaml`, set the address phones and Open5GS reach Ella IMS on, its Diameter host label, and the address it receives the PCF's notifications on, and restart Ella IMS:

```
sip:
  addresses: [10.0.0.20]
diameter:
  address: 10.0.0.20
  host_label: ims
n5:
  notify:
    address: 10.0.0.20
```

## 2. Add Open5GS as the HSS and PCF

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **Peers**, click **Create Peer**, enter `10.0.0.10`, check **HSS**, and click **Create**.
- Under **HSS**, click the edit icon next to **HSS Realm**, enter `localdomain`, and click **Update**.
- Under **Voice QoS**, click the edit icon next to **Policy Function**, select **PCF**, enter `http://10.0.0.10:7777` as the **PCF URI**, and click **Update**.

## 3. Route the phones' traffic

On the Ella IMS host, route the `ims` DNN through Open5GS's address:

```
sudo ip route add 10.45.0.0/16 via 10.0.0.10 mtu lock 1400
```

## 4. Configure Open5GS

At the end of `/etc/freeDiameter/hss.conf`, add Ella IMS as the peer `ims.ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`, with the MNC padded to 3 digits, e.g. for `001` / `01`:

```
ConnectPeer = "ims.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org" { ConnectTo = "10.0.0.20"; No_TLS; No_SCTP; };
```

In `/etc/open5gs/pcf.yaml`, change the address of `pcf.sbi.server` from `127.0.0.13` to `10.0.0.10`.

In `/etc/open5gs/smf.yaml`, under `smf`, add:

```
  p-cscf:
    - 10.0.0.20
```

Restart Open5GS:

```
sudo systemctl restart open5gs-hssd open5gs-pcfd open5gs-smfd
```

Exempt Ella IMS from the Quickstart's NAT rule:

```
sudo iptables -t nat -I POSTROUTING -s 10.45.0.0/16 -d 10.0.0.20 -j ACCEPT
```

## 5. Provision the subscribers

In the Open5GS WebUI, for each subscriber:

- Set the **MSISDN**.
- Add an `ims` DNN with 5QI `5` and ARP `1`.
- Under the `ims` DNN, add a PCC rule with 5QI `1`, ARP `2`, and MBR and GBR of `128` Kbps.

# Manage Single Sign-On Users

These guides manage users who sign in through the identity provider. [Configure single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/configure_single_sign_on/index.md) first.

## Give a user access

1. In the UI, go to **Users** and click **Create**. Set:
   - **Email**: the user's email address at the identity provider
   - **Password**: off
   - **Role**: the user's role
   - **Pin role**: checked to keep this role, if groups are mapped to roles
1. Click **Create**.

The user signs in with **Log in with** the display name. Their first login links their user to their account at the identity provider.

## Map groups to roles

Users in a mapped group get their role from it at each login, and get a user at their first login. Users in no mapped group cannot sign in through the identity provider, unless their role is [pinned](#pin-a-users-role).

### 1. Send groups to Ella IMS

1. Go to **Clients**, open the `ims` client, and open the **Client scopes** tab.
1. Click `ims-dedicated`, then **Configure a new mapper**, or **Add mapper** > **By configuration**, then **Group Membership**.
1. Set **Name** and **Token Claim Name** to `groups`. Turn off **Full group path**. Keep **Add to ID token** on.
1. Click **Save**.

The groups are group names, such as `ims-admins`.

Configure the provider to send the user's groups in a claim, such as `groups`, as a list of group names or IDs.

### 2. Map the groups in Ella IMS

1. Go to **Single Sign-On** and, in **Roles from groups**, click **Edit**.
1. Set **Groups claim** to `groups`.
1. Click **Add group** for each group, and set the group and its role. Put the most privileged first: a user in several groups gets the role of the first.
1. Click **Update**.

## Pin a user's role

A pinned role is kept whatever the user's groups.

1. Go to **Users** and open the user.
1. In **Account**, edit the role: choose the role, check **Pin role**, and click **Update**. Changing a role that comes from groups checks it for you.

To unpin, uncheck **Pin role**. The role then follows the user's groups from their next login.

## Unlink a user

Unlink a user whose account at the identity provider was replaced, so that their next login links the new account by email.

1. Go to **Users** and open the user.
1. In **Account**, click **Unlink**, then **Unlink**.

## Offboard a user

1. Remove or disable the user at the identity provider. They can no longer sign in, but their current session lasts until the **Session lifetime** ends.
1. To end their access at once, go to **Users** in Ella IMS, open the user, and click **Delete**. This also deletes their API tokens.

To keep the user instead, open the user and:

1. In **Account**, click **Unlink**, then **Unlink**. This ends their single sign-on sessions.
1. Click **Remove Password**, then **Remove**, if they have one.
1. In **API Tokens**, delete each token.

# Scale a High Availability Cluster

This guide walks through adding a node to an existing Ella IMS high-availability cluster, and removing one.

## Prerequisites

- A running HA cluster deployed (see [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md)).

## Add a node

1. Prepare a host with Ella IMS installed per the [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md) guide, with a `cluster` block in the configuration file.

1. Open the **Cluster** page on any node in the cluster.

1. Click **Add Node**, click **Create Token**, and copy the token.

1. Start Ella IMS on the new host.

1. Open the new node's UI in a browser. Click **Join an existing cluster instead**, paste the token, and click **Join**.

1. On the HSS and the PCRF, accept the new node's Diameter host. Add its SIP address to the P-CSCF addresses of the core network.

1. On the leader's **Cluster** page, verify the new node appears and is shown as **Healthy**.

1. Add a Kubernetes node for the new pod, with a second interface, as for the others.

1. Add a pod:

   ```
   kubectl scale statefulset ella-ims -n ella --replicas=4
   ```

1. On the HSS and the PCRF, accept the new pod's Diameter host. Add its SIP address to the P-CSCF addresses of the core network.

1. On the leader's **Cluster** page, verify the new node appears and is shown as **Healthy**.

## Remove a node

1. Open the leader's **Cluster** page.

1. In the node's **Node actions** menu, click **Drain this node**. Wait until its **Drain** column shows **Drained**.

1. In the same menu, click **Remove from cluster**. For a node that is down for good, check **Force remove (skip drain)**.

1. Remove the node from the HSS, the PCRF and the P-CSCF addresses of the core network.

1. Open the leader's **Cluster** page.

1. In the **Node actions** menu of the node with the highest pod number, click **Drain this node**. Wait until its **Drain** column shows **Drained**.

1. In the same menu, click **Remove from cluster**.

1. Remove its pod and volume:

   ```
   kubectl scale statefulset ella-ims -n ella --replicas=3
   kubectl delete pvc data-ella-ims-3 -n ella
   ```

1. Remove the node from the HSS, the PCRF and the P-CSCF addresses of the core network.

# Upgrade

## Prerequisites

- Ella IMS installed with [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/install/index.md) or [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md).
- The target release of `ella-ims` available.

## 1. Upgrade

Refresh the snap:

```
sudo snap refresh ella-ims
```

In the directory of `docker-compose.yaml`, pull the new image and restart the container:

```
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

1. Set the new image:

   ```
   kubectl set image statefulset/ella-ims -n ella ims=ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-ims:<version>
   ```

1. Wait for the rollout:

   ```
   kubectl rollout status statefulset/ella-ims -n ella
   ```

Repeat these steps for each node:

1. On that host, refresh the snap:

   ```
   sudo snap refresh ella-ims
   ```

1. On the leader's **Cluster** page, wait for the node to return to **Healthy**.

1. Set the new image:

   ```
   kubectl set image statefulset/ella-ims -n ella ims=ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-ims:<version>
   ```

1. Wait for the rollout:

   ```
   kubectl rollout status statefulset/ella-ims -n ella
   ```

## 2. Verify

Check the running version in the UI's top bar.

On the leader's **Cluster** page, confirm:

- Every node's **Version** column shows the target release.
- Every node is **Healthy** and its **Drain** column shows **Active**.
