# Configuration File

Ella IMS is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella IMS with the `--config` flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected.

## Parameters

- `logging` (object, optional): The logging configuration.
  - `level` (string, optional): The log level: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error`. Default `info`.
- `db` (object): The database configuration.
  - `path` (string): The path to the SQLite database file. Its directory also holds `node.db`, the node's own database, and `raft/`, the node's Raft log and identity.
- `api` (object): The HTTP API and UI.
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` or `::` for all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `5020`.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM private key.
- `sip` (object): SIP, for every CSCF.
  - `name` (string): The network interface whose addresses the CSCFs listen on and phones reach. Either `name` or `addresses` must be set.
  - `addresses` (list of strings): The IP addresses the CSCFs listen on and phones reach. Specific addresses, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`. Either `name` or `addresses` must be set.
  - `trusted_networks` (list of strings, optional): The networks, in CIDR notation, of the other nodes of the trust domain, such as Application Servers. The S-CSCF accepts requests only from them, the I-CSCF accepts their asserted identities, and Application Servers are sent requests only in them. Must not cover every address of a family. See [Security](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/security/#the-trust-domain).
- `pcscf` (object, optional): The P-CSCF.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default `5060`.
  - `ipsec` (object, optional): The IPsec ports.
    - `server_port` (int, optional): The protected server port. Default `5063`.
    - `client_ports` (list of 2 ints, optional): The protected client ports. Default `[5064, 5065]`.
- `icscf` (object, optional): The I-CSCF.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default `5070`.
- `scscf` (object, optional): The S-CSCF.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default `5080`.
  - `as_timeout` (duration, optional): How long an Application Server has to respond before the default handling of its iFC applies, e.g. `4s`. Under `32s`. Default `4s`.
- `diameter` (object): Diameter, to the HSS and the PCRF.
  - `name` (string): The network interface of the Diameter connections, on all its addresses, advertised to peers. Either `name` or `address` must be set.
  - `address` (string): The IP address of the Diameter connections, advertised to peers. A specific address, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`. Either `name` or `address` must be set.
  - `port` (int, optional): The port. Default `3868`.
  - `host_label` (string, optional): The first label of the node's [Diameter host](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/connectivity/#diameter-identity). Default `ims-` and the last 12 hex characters of the node ID.
- `n5` (object, optional): N5, to a PCF. Required to select the PCF as the policy function.
  - `notify` (object): Where the P-CSCF receives the PCF's notifications.
    - `address` (string): The IP address. A specific address, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`.
    - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port. `0`, the default, lets the system choose one. Must differ from the other TCP ports on its address.
  - `tls` (object, optional): Mutual TLS on N5. Required for a PCF URI with the `https` scheme. The files are read when the PCF URI is set.
    - `ca` (string): The path to the PEM file of the CA certificates that the PCF's certificate must chain to.
    - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM file of Ella IMS's certificate, presented as both client and server. Must be valid for `n5.notify.address`.
    - `key` (string): The path to the PEM file of the certificate's private key.
- `mcptt` (object, optional): The built-in MCPTT server. When absent, the MCPTT server doesn't run and opens no ports.
  - `mode` (string, optional): `ims`, the default, or `direct`: the MCPTT server is the registrar of its clients, without the IMS, for labs and tests.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port on each of `sip.addresses`. In `direct` mode, the UDP and TCP port clients send to. Default `5090`.
  - `media` (object): The media relay.
    - `address` (string): The IP address of the media sockets.
    - `advertise` (string, optional): The IP address in the SDP, of the same family as `address`. Required if `address` is `0.0.0.0` or `::`. Default `address`.
    - `min_port` (int, optional): The first port of the voice legs. Even. Default `20000`.
    - `max_port` (int, optional): The last port of the voice legs. Default `20999`.
    - `control_port` (int, optional): The port of the floor control channels, outside the voice legs' range. Default `21000`.
- `ibcf` (object, optional): The IBCF, the border towards [SIP trunks](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/sip_trunks/index.md). When absent, the IBCF doesn't run and opens no ports.
  - `port` (int, optional): The SIP port of the IBCF on each of `sip.addresses`, towards the I-CSCF and the S-CSCF. Default `5085`.
  - `external` (object): Where carriers reach Ella IMS, on SIP port `5060`, UDP and TCP, and TLS port `5061`.
    - `addresses` (list of objects): One IPv4 address, one IPv6 address, or one of each.
      - `address` (string): The IP address. A specific address, not `0.0.0.0` or `::`, neither in `sip.addresses` nor in `sip.trusted_networks`.
      - `advertise` (string, optional): The public address, of the same family, when Ella IMS is behind a 1:1 NAT that keeps ports. Default `address`.
    - `tls` (object, optional): Ella IMS's certificate, to accept TLS connections from carriers.
      - `cert` (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the leaf first.
      - `key` (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  - `media` (object, optional): The UDP ports of the voice of calls over SIP trunks, on `sip.addresses` and on `ibcf.external.addresses`. Two ports per call on each.
    - `min_port` (int, optional): The first port. Even, from `1024`. Default `10000`.
    - `max_port` (int, optional): The last port. Default `19999`.
- `cluster` (object, optional): The cluster port. Required to create or join a [cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/high_availability/index.md).
  - `address` (string): The IP address to listen on. `0.0.0.0` or `::` for all addresses, with `advertise` set.
  - `port` (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default `7000`.
  - `advertise` (string, optional): The `host:port` the other nodes reach this node at. A specific address or a host name. Default `address:port`.
  - `join` (list of strings, optional): The `host` or `host:port` of the other nodes, on `port` when the port is left out. Each name resolves to all its addresses.
  - `bootstrap_expect` (int, optional): The number of nodes that form a new cluster together. 2 or more. Requires `join`.
  - `secret_file` (string): The path to the cluster secret: base64 keys of at least 32 bytes, one per line, the first used to sign. Required with `join`.
- `telemetry` (object, optional): The [traces](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/observability/#traces).
  - `enabled` (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default `false`.
  - `otlp_endpoint` (string): The `host:port` of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when `enabled` is `true`.

## Example

```
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: ims.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5020
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
pcscf:
  port: 5060
  ipsec:
    server_port: 5063
    client_ports: [5064, 5065]
icscf:
  port: 5070
scscf:
  port: 5080
ibcf:
  port: 5085
  external:
    addresses:
      - address: 10.0.0.5
        advertise: 203.0.113.5
    tls:
      cert: /etc/ims/tls/ibcf.crt
      key: /etc/ims/tls/ibcf.key
  media:
    min_port: 10000
    max_port: 19999
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.5
  port: 3868
cluster:
  address: 10.0.0.1
  port: 7000
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp_endpoint: localhost:4317
```

# Connectivity

| Interface   | Address                                              | Peers                       | Ports                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API         | `api.address`                                        | Operators, Prometheus       | TCP `api.port` (`5020`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| SIP         | `sip.name` or `sip.addresses`                        | Phones, Application Servers | P-CSCF: UDP and TCP `pcscf.port` (`5060`) P-CSCF, IPsec: UDP and TCP in ESP, `pcscf.ipsec.server_port` (`5063`), `pcscf.ipsec.client_ports` (`5064`, `5065`) I-CSCF: UDP and TCP `icscf.port` (`5070`) S-CSCF: UDP and TCP `scscf.port` (`5080`) MCPTT, `direct` mode, or `ims` mode with a `cluster` block: UDP and TCP `mcptt.port` (`5090`) Voice of calls over SIP trunks: UDP `ibcf.media.min_port`–`max_port` (`10000`–`19999`) |
| Carriers    | `ibcf.external.addresses`                            | SIP trunks                  | SIP: UDP and TCP `5060`, TLS `5061` Voice: UDP `ibcf.media.min_port`–`max_port` (`10000`–`19999`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Diameter    | `diameter.name` or `diameter.address`                | HSS, PCRF, SMSC, MME, SMSF  | TCP or SCTP `diameter.port` (`3868`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| MCPTT media | `mcptt.media.address`                                | MCPTT clients               | UDP `mcptt.media.min_port`–`max_port` (`20000`–`20999`), `mcptt.media.control_port` (`21000`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| N5          | `n5.notify.address`                                  | PCF                         | HTTP/2, optionally with mutual TLS, `n5.notify.port` (chosen by the system)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Cluster     | `cluster.address`, advertised as `cluster.advertise` | The other Ella IMS nodes    | TCP, mutual TLS 1.3, `cluster.port` (`7000`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Defaults are in parentheses. The cluster port listens only when the configuration file has a `cluster` block.

In a cluster, the I-CSCF of each node sends requests to the S-CSCF of the other nodes, on their SIP addresses, over TCP or UDP `scscf.port`. The MCPTT server of each node sends requests to the MCPTT server of the other nodes, on their SIP addresses, over UDP or TCP `mcptt.port`. MCPTT clients send media to the MCPTT media address of any node. Each node trusts the SIP addresses of the other members.

On Kubernetes, the cluster address of node `<n>` is `ella-ims-<n>.ella-ims-internal.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`.

## Diameter identity

| Item  | Value                                           |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Host  | `<label>.ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org` |
| Realm | `ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`         |

`<MCC>` and `<MNC>` are the operator's, with a 2-digit MNC padded to 3. `<label>` is the node's `diameter.host_label`, by default `ims-` and the last 12 hex characters of the node ID.

# Environment Variables

These environment variables override parameters of the configuration file.

| Variable                  | Overrides                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `IMS_DIAMETER_HOST_LABEL` | `diameter.host_label` in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md)                                   |
| `IMS_CLUSTER_ADVERTISE`   | `cluster.advertise` in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md). Ignored without a `cluster` block. |

# Observability

Ella IMS supports four observability pillars: Metrics, Traces, Logs and Profiles.

## Metrics

Ella IMS exposes Prometheus metrics at `GET /api/v1/metrics`.

| Metric                                      | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ellaims_build_info`                        | Gauge                   | Always 1. The version and revision of the running build are in its labels.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ellaims_registered_subscribers`            | Gauge                   | Subscribers registered now on this node.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ellaims_registration_attempts_total`       | Counter                 | Registrations and re-registrations, by result: `accept`, `auth_failure`, `reject`.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ellaims_active_calls`                      | Gauge                   | Calls in progress.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ellaims_calls_total`                       | Counter                 | Calls that ended, by outcome: `answered`, `cancelled`, `busy`, `rejected`, `no_answer`, `unavailable`, `failed`.                                                                                                                   |
| `ellaims_sip_responses_total`               | Counter                 | Final responses the P-CSCF sent to phones, by method and status class.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `ellaims_sip_request_duration_seconds`      | Histogram               | Time from a request of a phone to the final response the P-CSCF sent, by method and status class, the answer of the far end included when the request is forwarded. `INVITE` is left out: its final response waits for the callee. |
| `ellaims_diameter_peer_up`                  | Gauge                   | 1 if the connection to a Diameter peer is open, by peer and application.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ellaims_peer_requests_total`               | Counter                 | Requests to the HSS, the policy function, the SMSCs and the MMEs and SMSFs, by interface (`cx`, `rx`, `n5`, `sh`, `s6c`, `sgd`) and result (`success`, `failure`, `error`, `timeout`).                                             |
| `ellaims_peer_request_duration_seconds`     | Histogram               | Duration of requests to the HSS, the policy function, the SMSCs and the MMEs and SMSFs, by interface.                                                                                                                              |
| `ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total`       | Counter                 | Short messages the IP-SM-GW carried, by direction (`mo`, `mt`), domain (`smsc` for `mo`; `ims`, `mme`, `sgsn`, `smsf_3gpp`, `smsf_non_3gpp`, `none` for `mt`, the last tried) and result (`success`, `failure`).                   |
| `ellaims_trunk_info`                        | Gauge                   | 1 per SIP trunk, by trunk ID and name.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `ellaims_trunk_up`                          | Gauge                   | 1 if a SIP trunk answers its OPTIONS keepalives, 0 if it is down, by trunk ID. A trunk without keepalives, disabled, or not probed yet, has no series.                                                                             |
| `ellaims_trunk_calls_total`                 | Counter                 | Calls over a SIP trunk that ended, by the ID of the trunk that gave the final answer, direction (`inbound`, `outbound`) and outcome, as `ellaims_calls_total`.                                                                     |
| `ellaims_trunk_active_calls`                | Gauge                   | Calls over a SIP trunk in progress, by trunk ID and direction.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ellaims_trunk_failovers_total`             | Counter                 | Calls to a SIP trunk retried on its next server or the next trunk of their route after a transport error, a timeout or a 503, by the ID of the trunk that failed.                                                                  |
| `ellaims_trunk_media_relays`                | Gauge                   | Media streams that the media relay of SIP trunks relays now, by trunk ID.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ellaims_trunk_media_packets_relayed_total` | Counter                 | RTP and RTCP packets that the media relay of SIP trunks relayed, by trunk ID, the leg they arrived on (`phone`, `trunk`) and protocol.                                                                                             |
| `ellaims_trunk_media_packets_dropped_total` | Counter                 | RTP and RTCP packets that the media relay of SIP trunks dropped, by trunk ID, leg and reason: `unexpected_source`, `no_remote`, `no_destination`, `direction`, `malformed`, `send_error`, `policed`.                               |
| `ellaims_trunk_media_packets_lost_total`    | Counter                 | RTP packets lost before reaching the media relay of SIP trunks, from gaps in sequence numbers, by trunk ID and leg.                                                                                                                |
| `ellaims_api_request_duration_seconds`      | Histogram               | Duration of API requests, by method, route (`/api/v1/users/{email}`) and status code. Requests to `/api/v1/pprof/` and to no route are left out.                                                                                   |
| `ellaims_oidc_logins_total`                 | Counter                 | Logins through the identity provider, by outcome: `success`, or a [login error](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/auth/#errors).                                                                                     |
| `ellaims_database_query_duration_seconds`   | Histogram               | Duration of database calls, by connection pool: `write`, `read`, `local`. Exemplars: `trace_id`, `span_id`.                                                                                                                        |
| `ellaims_database_query_errors_total`       | Counter                 | Failed database calls, by connection pool.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ellaims_database_storage_bytes`            | Gauge                   | Size of the databases on disk, by file: `main`, `wal`, `node`, `node_wal`.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ellaims_cluster_failure_tolerance`         | Gauge                   | Voters that can fail without stopping writes. Leader only.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ellaims_cluster_foreign_peers`             | Gauge                   | Nodes behind `cluster.join` that are members of another cluster.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ellaims_cluster_join_requests_total`       | Counter                 | Join and hello requests from other nodes, by result: `admitted`, `rejected`, `unauthorized`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`.                                                                                                        |
| `ellaims_ready_check`                       | Gauge                   | 1 when the readiness check passes, 0 when it fails, by [check](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/status/#checks) (`shutdown`, `member`, `initialized`, `diameter_label`, `drain`, `database`, `leader`).             |
| `go_*`                                      | Gauge, Counter, Summary | Go runtime: goroutines, heap, garbage-collection pauses.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `process_*`                                 | Gauge, Counter          | Process: memory, CPU, open file descriptors, start time.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `raft_*`                                    | Gauge, Counter, Summary | [hashicorp/raft](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft) metrics.                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Traces

Ella IMS exports [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) traces when `telemetry.enabled` is set in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md).

| Property         | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Export           | OTLP over gRPC, without TLS                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Service          | `ella-ims`                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Sampling         | Parent-based, always on for a trace the IMS starts                                                                                                                                                             |
| Propagation      | W3C Trace Context                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Error status     | HTTP and SIP: a server span from a 5xx response, a client span from a 4xx, except a SIP 401 or 407 challenge. Diameter: a client span from a Result-Code from 3000.                                            |
| SIP trust domain | Trace context is read and sent on SIP only within the trust domain: the IMS's own addresses, and for the I-CSCF, the S-CSCF and the MCPTT AS, `sip.trusted_networks`. It never reaches a phone or a SIP trunk. |

### Spans

| Span                                                                             | Kind           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{method} {route}`                                                               | Server         | A request to the API, except `/api/v1/livez`, `/api/v1/readyz`, `/api/v1/metrics` and `/api/v1/pprof/`. Links to the caller's `traceparent`.                                                                              |
| `{method} {url.template}`                                                        | Client         | A request to the PCF on N5.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `POST /n5/v1/sessions/{id}/{notify,terminate}`                                   | Server         | A notification from the PCF on N5.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Cx/{command}`, `Sh/{command}`, `Rx/{command}`, `S6c/{command}`, `SGd/{command}` | Server, Client | A Diameter request.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `{method}`, such as `INVITE`                                                     | Server, Client | A SIP transaction, until its final response. A request from a phone or a SIP trunk starts a trace, linked to the INVITE of its call or the REGISTER it renews. Out-of-dialog OPTIONS to and from SIP trunks have no span. |
| `registration expiry`, `media loss`, `media timeout`, …                          | Internal       | Work that starts later than its cause, as on a timer or after a settings change: a new trace, linked to its cause. `media timeout`: the IBCF ends a call whose media stopped, linked to its INVITE.                       |
| `db.{call}`, such as `db.SaveSet`                                                | Internal       | A database call within a trace.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `POST /cluster/v1/{propose,join,probe,hello}`                                    | Server, Client | A request between cluster nodes within a trace. `join` and `hello` from a node not yet in the cluster link to the caller's `traceparent`.                                                                                 |
| `raft wait applied`                                                              | Internal       | A follower applying a write it forwarded to the leader.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `raft apply`                                                                     | Internal       | A batch of writes committed to the Raft log, when one of its writes is in a sampled trace. A new trace, linked to the sampled spans of its writes.                                                                        |

## Logs

| Field      | Description                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `trace_id` | Trace ID of the span the event happened in. Absent outside a span. |
| `span_id`  | Span ID of the span the event happened in. Absent outside a span.  |

### Audit events

Audit events are logs at level `info` with `msg` set to `audit event`.

| Field     | Description                                               |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action`  | What was done, such as `auth_login` or `auth_oidc_login`. |
| `actor`   | Email of the user who did it. Empty when unknown.         |
| `ip`      | Address the request came from.                            |
| `details` | What was done, in words.                                  |

## Profiles

Ella IMS exposes the [net/http/pprof](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof) API at [`/api/v1/pprof/`](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/pprof/index.md).

# Performance

Measured capacity of the two hosts of the [system requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/system_reqs/index.md).

## Registrations

Registration time: from the initial REGISTER to its 200 OK, through the IMS-AKA challenge, measured at the phone (TS 32.409 §4.1.1.1). Once all are registered, each phone deregisters, then registers again.

### 1,000 Subscribers, 2 vCPU

| Load                                | Rate (/s) | Initial registration success rate | Mean  | p99    | CPU (cores) |
| ----------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ----------- |
| From 0 to 1,000 registered, in 10 s | 100       | 100%                              | 29 ms | 307 ms | —           |
| 1,000 registered                    | 10        | 100%                              | 9 ms  | 30 ms  | 0.21        |
| 1,000 registered                    | 25        | 100%                              | 8 ms  | 23 ms  | 0.52        |
| 1,000 registered                    | 50        | 100%                              | 19 ms | 41 ms  | 0.97        |

### 50,000 Subscribers, 16 vCPU

| Load                                       | Rate (/s) | Initial registration success rate | Mean  | p99    | CPU (cores) |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------- | --------------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ----------- |
| From 0 to 50,000 registered, in 8 min 20 s | 100       | 100%                              | 18 ms | 98 ms  | —           |
| 50,000 registered                          | 50        | 100%                              | 42 ms | 1.04 s | 0.93        |
| 50,000 registered                          | 100       | 100%                              | 51 ms | 1.07 s | 1.72        |
| 50,000 registered                          | 150       | 10%                               | 5.1 s | 23.6 s | 0.99        |

### Re-registrations

Each subscriber re-registers every 3,000 s (TS 24.229 §5.1.1.4.1), during the calls.

| Subscribers | Rate (/s) | Re-registration success rate | Mean  | p99    |
| ----------- | --------- | ---------------------------- | ----- | ------ |
| 1,000       | 0.33      | 100%                         | 6 ms  | 21 ms  |
| 50,000      | 16.7      | 100%                         | 27 ms | 122 ms |

## Calls

Voice calls with preconditions (IR.92 §2.4.1), answered at once and held 90 s. Session setup time: from the INVITE to the first 180 or 2xx, measured at the calling phone (TS 32.409 §4.1.2.6).

### 1,000 Subscribers, 2 vCPU

| Rate (/s) | Calls per hour | Session establishment success rate | Call drop rate | Session setup time, mean | p99   | Calls in progress | CPU (cores) | Resident memory |
| --------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ | ----- | ----------------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| 2         | 7,200          | 100%                               | 0%             | 15 ms                    | 23 ms | 181               | 0.05        | 211 MiB         |
| 5         | 18,000         | 100%                               | 0%             | 16 ms                    | 31 ms | 451               | 0.10        | 267 MiB         |

### 50,000 Subscribers, 16 vCPU

| Rate (/s) | Calls per hour | Session establishment success rate | Call drop rate | Session setup time, mean | p99    | Calls in progress | CPU (cores) | Resident memory |
| --------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------ | ------ | ----------------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| 25        | 90,000         | 100%                               | 0%             | 54 ms                    | 155 ms | 2,255             | 0.61        | 4.0 GiB         |
| 50        | 180,000        | 100%                               | 0%             | 55 ms                    | 144 ms | 4,501             | 1.00        | 4.6 GiB         |
| 100       | 360,000        | 100%                               | 0%             | 41 ms                    | 126 ms | 9,009             | 1.78        | 6.0 GiB         |

## Memory

| Item                                      | Value                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Resident memory, idle                     | 30 MiB                    |
| Resident memory per registered subscriber | 71 KiB                    |
| Kernel memory per registered subscriber   | 26 KiB                    |
| Memory of ended calls                     | Released within 2 minutes |

## Limits

| Limit                  | Value                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Registered subscribers | 50,000 tested                                                                                         |
| Registration rate      | Set by the disk's write IOPS: 100/s with 3,000, 150/s with 5,800. Beyond it, most registrations fail. |
| SIP TCP connections    | 3/4 of the open-file limit: 393,216 at systemd's default of 524,288. Each phone uses up to 2.         |
| MCPTT users            | 1,000                                                                                                 |

On Linux 6.13 and later, the kernel's processing of incoming IPsec traffic grows with the number of registered phones.

## Host Requirements

| Requirement    | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Receive queues | A receive queue per CPU, or, with a single receive queue, Receive Packet Steering (RPS) on all CPUs: `/sys/class/net/<interface>/queues/rx-0/rps_cpus`. Otherwise one CPU processes all incoming traffic. |

## Test Setup

| Item                     | Value                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Version                  | Ella IMS built from source, after v0.0.1, default configuration                                                                                                    |
| Host, 1,000 subscribers  | Google Cloud `n2-custom-2-4096`: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM                                                                                                                  |
| Host, 50,000 subscribers | Google Cloud `n2-highcpu-16`: 16 vCPU, 16 GB RAM                                                                                                                   |
| Operating system         | Ubuntu 26.04, Linux 7.0 (`7.0.0-1014-gcp`)                                                                                                                         |
| Network                  | `virtio_net`, one receive queue per vCPU                                                                                                                           |
| Disk                     | Google Cloud `pd-balanced`, 30 GB: 3,000 IOPS                                                                                                                      |
| Open-file limit          | 1,048,576                                                                                                                                                          |
| Load generator           | Separate VM in the same zone: `n2-standard-4` for 1,000 subscribers, `n2-standard-16` for 50,000                                                                   |
| Phones                   | Simulated: IMS-AKA, IPsec with integrity protection only (`hmac-sha-1-96`, no encryption), SIP over TCP, one IP address per phone, registration event subscription |
| Re-registrations         | Not re-authenticated (S-CSCF default)                                                                                                                              |
| HSS                      | Simulated, over Cx, on the load generator: 1.7 ms mean response time with 1,000 subscribers, 2.8 ms with 50,000                                                    |
| Policy                   | Simulated PCRF, over Rx, on the load generator: 0.6 ms mean response time with 1,000 subscribers, 3.8 ms with 50,000                                               |
| Media                    | Not carried by Ella IMS                                                                                                                                            |

# Supported Mobile Equipment

Ella IMS follows 3GPP standards. Any compliant core network, Application Server and phone should work with it. This page lists those validated against Ella IMS.

## Core Networks

- **[Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/)**
- **[Open5GS](https://open5gs.org/)**

## Phones

- **Apple iPhone 11**
- **Apple iPhone 16**
- **Crosscall Core-Z5**
- **Google Pixel 10a**
- **Motorola Moto G 5G**
- **Samsung Galaxy A56**

## MCPTT Clients

- **Ella MCPTT for Android**, in the [`android`](https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/tree/main/android) directory.

## Phone Quirks

| Phone              | RAT | Observed                                                                           |
| ------------------ | --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Apple iPhone 11    | 4G  | Live Voicemail answers declined and unanswered calls (`200 OK`).                   |
| Apple iPhone 16    | 4G  | Live Voicemail answers declined and unanswered calls (`200 OK`).                   |
|                    | 4G  | 3 IMS addresses in 6 minutes.                                                      |
|                    | 4G  | No video calls: registers with `audio` only, no `video` feature tag.               |
|                    | 5G  | 5G SA unavailable without SUCI on the SIM (USIM service 124, `EF.SUCI_Calc_Info`). |
|                    | 5G  | Rejects NEA0 (Security Mode Reject, cause 24).                                     |
|                    | 5G  | SIM PLMN 001/01: never attempts the 5G SA cell.                                    |
|                    | 5G  | SIM PLMN 999/01: data only, no voice settings, no IMS PDU session.                 |
| Google Pixel 10a   | 4G  | Video call to an iPhone: the dialer offers Google Meet instead.                    |
| Motorola Moto G 5G | 5G  | SIM PLMN 999/01: 5G SA only with network type "NR only".                           |
|                    | 5G  | Video call answered without a camera, then switched to `recvonly` (once in 5).     |
|                    | 4G  | SIM PLMN 999/01: IMS doesn't start.                                                |
| Samsung Galaxy A56 | 4G  | SIM PLMN 001/01: VoLTE off (`LABSIM` profile, TS.43 entitlement 403).              |

# System Requirements

Ella IMS runs on Linux. It supports **amd64** and **arm64** architectures.

|                      | Up to 1,000 subscribers                                                                         | Up to 50,000 subscribers                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CPU**              | 2 cores                                                                                         | 16 cores                                                                                        |
| **Memory**           | 4 GB RAM                                                                                        | 16 GB RAM                                                                                       |
| **Disk**             | SSD, 3,000 write IOPS                                                                           | SSD, 3,000 write IOPS                                                                           |
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS                                                                                | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS                                                                                |
| **Kernel**           | IPsec: `xfrm_user`, `esp4`, `esp6` for IPv6, and `authenc`. SCTP, for Diameter peers over SCTP. | IPsec: `xfrm_user`, `esp4`, `esp6` for IPv6, and `authenc`. SCTP, for Diameter peers over SCTP. |
| **Network**          | Incoming traffic processed on all CPUs                                                          | Incoming traffic processed on all CPUs                                                          |
| **Privileges**       | `CAP_NET_ADMIN`                                                                                 | `CAP_NET_ADMIN`                                                                                 |
| **Kubernetes nodes** | SCTP kernel module                                                                              | SCTP kernel module                                                                              |

Both are measured, with room for registration bursts and calls: see the [performance reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/performance/index.md).

# API

## Authentication

Requests send a token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The token is either:

- an access token, from [log in](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/auth/#log-in) or [refresh the access token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/auth/#refresh-the-access-token), valid for 15 minutes;
- an [API token](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/users/#create-an-api-token), which starts with `ellaims_`.

These paths take no token: `GET /api/v1/livez`, `GET /api/v1/readyz`, `GET /api/v1/status`, `GET /api/v1/metrics`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml`, `POST /api/v1/init`, `POST /api/v1/cluster/join`, `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, `/refresh` and `/logout`, and `GET /api/v1/auth/oidc`, `/oidc/login` and `/oidc/callback`.

### Roles

| Role            | `role_id` | Allows                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Admin           | `1`       | Everything.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Read Only       | `2`       | Reading the settings, the registrations, the call records, the MCPTT state and the [cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/index.md). |
| Network Manager | `3`       | Read Only, plus changing the settings and re-authenticating registrations.                                                                                      |

Only an Admin manages users and the [cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/index.md), and [backs up and restores](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/backup/index.md). Every user reads its own user, changes its own password, and manages its own API tokens.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users or [single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/index.md).

## Responses

Ella IMS's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a `result`:

```
{
    "result": "Result content"
}
```

A failed response carries an `error`:

```
{
    "error": "Error message"
}
```

`GET /api/v1/livez` answers 204 with no body. `GET /api/v1/metrics` returns text in the [Prometheus exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#text-format-details), `GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml` returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

## OpenAPI Specification

The full API is described by an [OpenAPI 3.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0) specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella IMS instance:

```
GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml
```

## Status codes

- 200 - Success.
- 201 - Created.
- 202 - Accepted.
- 204 - No content.
- 400 - Bad request.
- 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
- 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
- 404 - Not found.
- 405 - Method not allowed.
- 409 - Conflict.
- 410 - The node was removed from the cluster. See [Remove a Member](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/#remove-a-member).
- 429 - Too many requests. `Retry-After` is the seconds to wait.
- 500 - Internal server error.
- 502 - The identity provider cannot be reached or used, see [Test an identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#test-an-identity-provider), or no cluster member answered a join, see [Join a Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/#join-a-cluster).
- 503 - Service unavailable, or not ready. See [Check readiness](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/status/#check-readiness).

# Authentication

## Log In

This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, `ims_session`, or `__Host-ims_session` over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

| Method | Path                 |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/login` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description                 |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `email`    | string | Yes      | Email address, in any case. |
| `password` | string | Yes      | Password.                   |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | Wrong email or password.                                                                                                                 |
| `429` | More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Refresh the Access Token

This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/refresh` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                       |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401` | No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}
```

## Log Out

This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

| Method | Path                  |
| ------ | --------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/auth/logout` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                |
| ----- | -------------------------- |
| `204` | Logged out, or no session. |

## Get the Single Sign-On Option

This path tells the login page whether to show the button to sign in through the identity provider.

| Method | Path                |
| ------ | ------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/auth/oidc` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak"
    }
}
```

## Sign In Through the Identity Provider

The login page sends the browser to this path, which redirects it to the identity provider. It counts toward the login limit of 20 per minute per address.

| Method | Path                      |
| ------ | ------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/auth/oidc/login` |

## Return From the Identity Provider

The identity provider sends the browser back to this path, the redirect URL. Each login completes once. On success, it sets the session cookie, for the [session lifetime](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#get-the-oidc-settings), and redirects to `/`. Otherwise, it redirects to `/login?error=<error>`, and the `auth_oidc_login` [audit event](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/observability/#audit-events) gives the details.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback` |

### Errors

| Error                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rate_limited`       | Too many logins from the address.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `unavailable`        | Single sign-on is off, or the identity provider cannot be reached.                                                                                                                            |
| `failed`             | The login expired, was already used or is invalid, the single sign-on settings changed during it, or the identity provider returned an error.                                                 |
| `denied`             | The user or the identity provider refused access.                                                                                                                                             |
| `not_set_up`         | The identity provider gives no email, or no user has it and no group mapping is set.                                                                                                          |
| `email_not_verified` | The identity provider marks the email as not verified, or does not say and [`trust_unverified_email`](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#update-the-oidc-settings) is off. |
| `linked_elsewhere`   | The user with the email is linked to another account at the identity provider.                                                                                                                |
| `no_group`           | None of the user's groups is mapped to a role.                                                                                                                                                |
| `groups_overage`     | The user is in too many groups for the identity provider to list them.                                                                                                                        |
| `too_many_users`     | 50 users exist.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `error`              | Internal error.                                                                                                                                                                               |

# Backup

A backup holds the settings, users and call records. It leaves out the secrets and the API sessions. It leaves out the registrations, which each node keeps on its own.

Both paths require Admin. Backing up accepts API tokens. Restoring requires an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Back Up

This path returns a backup of the database.

| Method | Path             |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/backup` |

### Response

A gzipped tar archive, with `Content-Type: application/gzip` and its file name in `Content-Disposition`, such as `ims-backup-20261104T120000Z.tar.gz`.

| File            | Description                                        |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest.json` | Format, schema version and time of the backup.     |
| `SHA256SUMS`    | SHA-256 checksums of `ims.db` and `manifest.json`. |
| `ims.db`        | The database.                                      |

## Restore

This path replaces the settings, users and call records with those of a backup, on every node of a cluster. The cluster keeps its nodes and its secrets, and each node keeps its registrations.

| Method | Path              |
| ------ | ----------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/restore` |

### Request Body

An archive from [Back Up](#back-up), with `Content-Type: application/gzip`.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Backup restored successfully"
    }
}
```

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400` | Not a backup, a checksum does not match, or the backup's schema is newer than this version's.                                    |
| `421` | The node is not the leader. See [Leader-Only Paths](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/#leader-only-paths). |
| `503` | No leader, or not ready to restore. Retry.                                                                                       |

# Call Records

A call record describes a call the IMS handled, after TS 32.298 §5.1.3.1.

## List Call Records

This path returns the list of call records, most recently requested first.

| Method | Path                   |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/call-records` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed                                                                           | Description                                                                  |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search`   | query | str  |         |                                                                                   | Substring of the ICID or of an identity of the caller or the callee.         |
| `start`    | query | str  |         |                                                                                   | Inclusive lower bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. |
| `end`      | query | str  |         |                                                                                   | Exclusive upper bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. |
| `outcome`  | query | str  |         | `answered`, `cancelled`, `busy`, `rejected`, `no_answer`, `unavailable`, `failed` | Outcome to include. Repeatable.                                              |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`                                                                            | 1-based page index.                                                          |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100`                                                                           | Number of items per page.                                                    |

### Response Fields

| Field               | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | int     | Record identifier.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `icid`              | string  | icid-value of the P-Charging-Vector (§5.1.3.1.19).                                                                                                                                     |
| `session_id`        | string  | Call-ID of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.59).                                                                                                                                                   |
| `calling_party`     | array   | P-Asserted-Identity values (§5.1.3.1.24).                                                                                                                                              |
| `caller_impi`       | string  | Private user identity of the caller (§5.1.3.1.36).                                                                                                                                     |
| `requested_party`   | string  | Request-URI from the caller (§5.1.3.1.43).                                                                                                                                             |
| `called_party`      | string  | Request-URI after normalisation by the S-CSCF (§5.1.3.1.9).                                                                                                                            |
| `callee_impi`       | string  | Private user identity of the answering registration (§5.1.3.1.36).                                                                                                                     |
| `requested_at`      | string  | Reception time of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.58).                                                                                                                                            |
| `delivery_start_at` | string  | Time of the final response to the caller (§5.1.3.1.55).                                                                                                                                |
| `delivery_end_at`   | string  | End time of an answered call (§5.1.3.1.54).                                                                                                                                            |
| `sip_status`        | int     | Final status of the INVITE sent to the caller (§5.1.3.1.57).                                                                                                                           |
| `outcome`           | string  | `answered` (2xx), `cancelled` (487 to a caller CANCEL), `busy` (486, 600), `rejected` (603), `no_answer` (408 after a 180), `unavailable` (480), or `failed` (any other final status). |
| `ended_by`          | string  | `caller`, `callee` or `network`.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `alerted`           | boolean | Whether a 180 reached the caller.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `media`             | array   | Media types of the accepted m-lines.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `in_progress`       | boolean | Whether the call has not ended.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `incomplete`        | boolean | Whether the record was closed without the end of the call.                                                                                                                             |
| `duration_ms`       | int     | Duration of an answered call that ended, in milliseconds.                                                                                                                              |
| `in_trunk_id`       | string  | ID of the SIP trunk the call came from. Absent for a call from a phone.                                                                                                                |
| `in_trunk_name`     | string  | Name of that SIP trunk at the time of the call.                                                                                                                                        |
| `out_trunk_id`      | string  | ID of the SIP trunk that gave the final answer. Absent for a call to a phone.                                                                                                          |
| `out_trunk_name`    | string  | Name of that SIP trunk at the time of the call.                                                                                                                                        |

A value the IMS did not observe is absent. Times are RFC 3339.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 42,
                "icid": "1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b",
                "session_id": "a84b4c76e66710@10.45.0.2",
                "calling_party": [
                    "sip:+15550000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                    "tel:+15550000001"
                ],
                "caller_impi": "001010000000001@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "requested_party": "tel:15550000002",
                "called_party": "tel:+15550000002",
                "callee_impi": "001010000000002@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
```
