# Status

## Get the Status

This path returns the version of the IMS, whether it has been initialized, and the identity of the node that answered. It takes no token.

| Method | Path             |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/status` |

### Response Fields

| Field             | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`         | string  | Version.                                                                                                                                     |
| `revision`        | string  | Git commit of the build. Empty in development builds.                                                                                        |
| `initialized`     | boolean | Whether the first user exists. Until then, [initialize](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/initialize/index.md) Ella IMS.       |
| `clustered`       | boolean | Whether the configuration file has a `cluster` block.                                                                                        |
| `node_id`         | string  | ID of the node that answered.                                                                                                                |
| `display_name`    | string  | Display name of the node. Empty when unset. See [Update a Member](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/#update-a-member). |
| `diameter_label`  | string  | First label of the node's Diameter host.                                                                                                     |
| `diameter_host`   | string  | Diameter host of the node.                                                                                                                   |
| `label_generated` | boolean | Whether `diameter_label` is the default, from `node_id`.                                                                                     |
| `formation`       | object  | See [Formation](#formation).                                                                                                                 |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "version": "v0.0.1",
        "revision": "",
        "initialized": true,
        "clustered": false,
        "node_id": "01a1ac75-e354-762b-b38f-013c0a7ca824",
        "display_name": "",
        "diameter_label": "ims-013c0a7ca824",
        "diameter_host": "ims-013c0a7ca824.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "label_generated": true,
        "formation": {
            "state": "member"
        }
    }
}
```

### Formation

| Field      | Type   | Description                                    |
| ---------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `state`    | string | `forming`, `joining`, `member` or `removed`.   |
| `expected` | int    | `cluster.bootstrap_expect`. Absent when unset. |
| `found`    | int    | Nodes found, this one included. While forming. |
| `detail`   | string | What the node is waiting for.                  |

## Check Liveness

This path answers while the process serves HTTP. It takes no token.

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/livez` |

It answers `204 No Content`.

## Check Readiness

This path returns whether the node is ready to receive traffic, and the result of each check. It takes no token.

| Method | Path             |
| ------ | ---------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/readyz` |

### Query Parameters

| Name      | Type    | Description                               |
| --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `cluster` | boolean | Add the `cluster` check. Default `false`. |

### Checks

| Name             | Passes when                                                                 |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shutdown`       | The node is not stopping.                                                   |
| `member`         | The node was not removed from the cluster, and is not forming one.          |
| `initialized`    | The node has no `cluster` block, or a user exists.                          |
| `diameter_label` | The cluster recorded this node's Diameter host label.                       |
| `drain`          | The node is not draining or drained.                                        |
| `database`       | The database answers.                                                       |
| `leader`         | The node leads, or heard from the leader within twice the election timeout. |
| `cluster`        | The node leads, and every voter is healthy. Only with `cluster=true`.       |

### Response Fields

| Field             | Type    | Description                         |
| ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `ready`           | boolean | Whether every check passes.         |
| `checks`          | array   | The checks, in order.               |
| `checks[].name`   | string  | Name of the check.                  |
| `checks[].ok`     | boolean | Whether it passes.                  |
| `checks[].detail` | string  | Why it fails. Empty when it passes. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                         |
| ----- | ----------------------------------- |
| `200` | Every check passes.                 |
| `400` | `cluster` is not `true` or `false`. |
| `503` | A check fails.                      |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "ready": false,
        "checks": [
            {"name": "shutdown", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "member", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "initialized", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "diameter_label", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "drain", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "database", "ok": true, "detail": ""},
            {"name": "leader", "ok": false, "detail": "no contact with the cluster leader for 12s"}
        ]
    }
}
```

# Users

Paths under `/api/v1/users/me` act on the user of the token. The others require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets `403`.

## Get My User

| Method | Path               |
| ------ | ------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/me` |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "role_id": 1,
        "role_pinned": false,
        "password_set": true,
        "oidc_linked": false
    }
}
```

### Response Fields

| Field          | Type    | Description                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`        | string  | Email address.                                                                                                                      |
| `role_id`      | int     | `1` to `3`. See [roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/#roles).                                                    |
| `role_pinned`  | boolean | The role is kept whatever the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles).                   |
| `password_set` | boolean | The user has a password.                                                                                                            |
| `oidc_linked`  | boolean | The user is linked to an account at the current [identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/index.md). |

The other paths that return users return the same fields.

## Update My Password

This path ends the user's other sessions. It requires an access token.

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/me/password` |

### Request Body

| Field              | Type   | Required | Description                  |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| `current_password` | string | Yes      | Current password.            |
| `password`         | string | Yes      | New password, 8 to 72 bytes. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                       |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400` | Wrong current password, or invalid new password.                                  |
| `409` | The user has no password.                                                         |
| `429` | More than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account, counting failed logins. |

## List Users

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "email": "admin@example.com",
                "role_id": 1,
                "role_pinned": false,
                "password_set": true,
                "oidc_linked": false
            },
            {
                "email": "noc@example.com",
                "role_id": 2,
                "role_pinned": false,
                "password_set": true,
                "oidc_linked": false
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 2
    }
}
```

## Create a User

At most 50 users.

| Method | Path            |
| ------ | --------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/users` |

### Request Body

| Field         | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`       | string  | Yes      | Email address. ASCII letters are stored in lower case.                                                                                            |
| `password`    | string  | No       | 8 to 72 bytes. Without it, the user signs in only through the [identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/index.md). |
| `role_id`     | int     | Yes      | `1` to `3`. See [roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/#roles).                                                                  |
| `role_pinned` | boolean | No       | Keep the role whatever the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles). Default `false`.                   |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                        |
| ----- | ---------------------------------- |
| `201` | Created.                           |
| `400` | Invalid field, or 50 users exist.  |
| `409` | A user has the email, in any case. |

## Get a User

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

## Update a User

This path sets the role of a user. A role change ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot change its own role, and the last Admin with a password stays an Admin.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Request Body

| Field         | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `role_id`     | int     | Yes      | `1` to `3`.                                                                                                                                           |
| `role_pinned` | boolean | No       | Keep the role whatever the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles). Without it, the current value is kept. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `409` | The role comes from the user's [groups](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/#group-roles) and `role_pinned` is not `true`, or the user is the last Admin with a password. |

## Update a User's Password

This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Request Body

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description    |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| `password` | string | Yes      | 8 to 72 bytes. |

## Remove a User's Password

This path removes the password of a user, who can then sign in only through the [identity provider](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/oidc/index.md). It ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot remove its own password, and the last Admin with a password keeps it.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/password` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                     |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `409` | The user has no password, or is the last Admin with a password. |

## Unlink a User

This path unlinks a user from their account at the identity provider, and ends the sessions started through it. Their next login through the identity provider links them again by email. An Admin cannot unlink itself.

| Method | Path                         |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/oidc` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                                                        |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `404` | No user has the email, or the user is not linked to the current identity provider. |

## Delete a User

This path deletes the user with its sessions and API tokens. An Admin cannot delete itself, and the last Admin with a password cannot be deleted.

| Method | Path                    |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}` |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                                 |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `409` | The user is the last Admin with a password. |

## Create an API Token

This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens`      |
| POST   | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens` |

### Request Body

| Field        | Type   | Required | Description                                                         |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | string | Yes      | 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens.                 |
| `expires_at` | string | No       | RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire. |

### Response Codes

| Code  | Description                        |
| ----- | ---------------------------------- |
| `201` | Created.                           |
| `400` | Invalid field, or 12 tokens exist. |
| `409` | The user has a token of that name. |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "Monitoring",
    "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "token": "ellaims_aB3dE5fG7hJ9_KQ4ZN2X7WJ5R3TQY6PLM2VA4CF"
    }
}
```

## List API Tokens

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens`      |
| GET    | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Response Fields

| Field          | Type   | Description                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | string | Token identifier: the part of the token between `ellaims_` and the next `_`. |
| `name`         | string | Name.                                                                        |
| `created_at`   | string | Creation time.                                                               |
| `expires_at`   | string | Expiry time. Absent for a token that does not expire.                        |
| `last_used_at` | string | Time of the last use, to the minute. Absent for a token never used.          |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "aB3dE5fG7hJ9",
                "name": "Monitoring",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:44:19.436Z",
                "expires_at": "2027-10-27T00:00:00.000Z",
                "last_used_at": "2026-10-27T19:02:00.000Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Delete an API Token

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/me/api-tokens/{id}`      |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens/{id}` |
# Explanation

# Explanation

These explanations provide context on how Ella IMS works.

- [Architecture](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/architecture/index.md)
- [Security](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/security/index.md)
- [Single Sign-On](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/single_sign_on/index.md)
- [Push-to-Talk](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/push_to_talk/index.md)
- [SMS over IP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/sms_over_ip/index.md)
- [SIP Trunks](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/sip_trunks/index.md)
- [High Availability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/high_availability/index.md)

# Architecture

Ella IMS with Ella Core

An IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) is what lets phones on a 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. The core network gives each phone an IP connection to the IMS. Over that connection, the phone registers and places calls with SIP, and the IMS routes them.

Ella IMS handles the signalling. The voice and video of a call go between the phones, through the core network. Calls over SIP trunks are the exception: their voice goes through Ella IMS.

## Three CSCFs in one process

3GPP splits the IMS's SIP routing into three Call Session Control Functions (CSCFs):

- **P-CSCF**: the phone's first contact. It protects the phone's signalling with IPsec, and asks the core network for the QoS that voice and video need.
- **I-CSCF**: the entry point of the network. It asks the HSS which S-CSCF serves a user.
- **S-CSCF**: the registrar. It authenticates phones against the HSS, routes calls, and involves Application Servers when a subscriber's filter criteria say so.

In most IMS deployments, these are separate nodes. Ella IMS runs all three in one process, with one database, one UI and one API. Each CSCF still has its own SIP port, and the three exchange standard SIP messages, in memory, so from the outside Ella IMS looks like any other IMS.

## What Ella IMS relies on

Ella IMS relies on two functions of the core network:

- **The HSS** holds the subscribers: their identities, the keys to authenticate them, and the filter criteria that bring in Application Servers. Ella IMS reaches it over Diameter (Cx).
- **The policy function** has the core set up the dedicated bearers (4G) or QoS flows (5G) that carry voice and video. Ella IMS reaches it over Diameter (Rx), or a PCF over HTTP (N5).

Ella Core provides both. For how it works with an IMS, see Ella Core's [IMS Integration](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/ims_integration/).

## Who can call whom

Ella IMS connects calls between the subscribers its HSS knows. Calls to and from other numbers go over SIP trunks, to carriers such as PSTN providers or other operators. See [SIP Trunks](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/sip_trunks/index.md).

Ella IMS does not handle emergency calls.

# High Availability

High availability (HA) lets you run an Ella IMS cluster so that the IMS keeps working when nodes fail. Each node is active and serves phones.

HA is designed around the [Raft Consensus Algorithm](https://raft.github.io/): at any time one node is the leader, it is the only node that commits writes, and every write replicates to a majority of voters before it is considered committed. Nodes communicate together via mTLS to share changes.

## Failure tolerance

A cluster keeps accepting writes as long as a majority of its voters are alive. Deploy 3 or 5 nodes.

| Voters | Quorum | Failures tolerated |
| ------ | ------ | ------------------ |
| 3      | 2      | 1                  |
| 5      | 3      | 2                  |

Without a majority, phones keep registering and calling. Only changes to settings and users, and new MCPTT group calls, stop.

## What replicates, and what does not

Settings, users, SIP trunks, MCPTT groups and affiliations, call records and the cluster's members replicate across the cluster.

Registrations, IPsec security associations and calls do not. Each node keeps those of the phones it serves.

Per-node configuration (addresses, ports, Diameter host label) does not replicate. Configure it on every node.

Observability is per-node: the UI and API show the registrations, live calls and SIP trunk status of the node that answers, and each node exposes its own metrics.

## Failover

A phone registers through one node, which serves it. A call to that phone can arrive on any node, which forwards it to the phone's node.

When a node dies, its calls drop. Its phones register again through another node. This requires an HSS that supports IMS restoration.

## SIP trunks

Each node connects to the carrier on its own, so the carrier must accept every node's address.

## Draining a node

Draining prepares a node for removal: phones register through other nodes at their next re-registration, and the node hands over the leadership.

Drain is triggered by an operator via the cluster API or UI.

## Inter-node communication using mTLS

Every inter-node connection is mutually authenticated over TLS. Removing a node immediately revokes its access cluster-wide.

## Disaster recovery

If a majority of the voters are lost for good, restore the last backup on a new cluster. See [Back Up and Restore](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/back_up_and_restore/index.md).

## Rolling upgrades

Upgrades proceed one node at a time. A restarted node keeps its registrations, so its phones stay registered. Downgrades are not supported.

## Further reading

- [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md)
- [Scale a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/scale_ha_cluster/index.md)
- [Upgrade](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/upgrade/index.md)
- [Cluster API](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/cluster/index.md)

# Push-to-Talk

Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) is the 3GPP standard for group calls where one member talks at a time and the others listen. Ella IMS includes an MCPTT server, which runs in the same process as the CSCFs. Unlike a regular call, a group call's voice goes through Ella IMS, which copies each talker's audio to every listener.

## Users and groups

A "user" is a person, such as `alice`. A "group" gathers users who talk together, such as a team.

A user hears and talks in a group's calls once their app has joined the group.

# Security

## Authenticating phones

Phones authenticate with the keys on their SIM, with IMS-AKA. When a phone registers, the S-CSCF fetches an authentication vector from the HSS, challenges the phone, and checks its answer. The phone checks the network in turn, so each side proves itself to the other.

## Protecting signalling with IPsec

The same authentication produces keys that the phone and the P-CSCF use to set up IPsec between them. From then on, the phone's SIP messages travel in ESP on dedicated ports. This protects the signalling from tampering, and ties every request to the phone that authenticated.

Ella IMS sets up these IPsec associations in the Linux kernel. That's why it needs `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, and why ESP must reach it through any firewall.

## The trust domain

SIP nodes tell each other who a request is from, for example with the `P-Asserted-Identity` header. A node believes this only from the nodes it trusts: its trust domain.

Phones are never trusted: the P-CSCF takes a phone's identity from its authentication.

Besides Ella IMS itself, the I-CSCF and the S-CSCF trust the networks in `sip.trusted_networks`, such as those of Application Servers. Trust goes by source address, so protect these networks, and keep the phones out of them.

## SIP trunks

Ella IMS accepts requests from a carrier only from its trunk's inbound CIDRs. Carriers are outside the trust domain, unless their trunk is trusted.

With TLS, Ella IMS checks the carrier's certificate on connections it opens to the carrier. With **TLS** > **Required**, it also checks the carrier's certificate on connections the carrier opens.

## Users of the UI and API

Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role. See [Roles](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/api/#roles). Programs, such as a monitoring system, use an API token instead of a password.

Users can also log in through the organization's identity provider. See [Single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/explanation/single_sign_on/index.md).

Until Ella IMS is initialized, anyone who reaches the UI can make themselves Admin, so initialize it right after installing.

## HTTPS

Ella IMS serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in `api.tls` (see the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md)). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

# Single Sign-On

Users can log in to the UI through the organization's identity provider instead of, or as well as, a password. Ella IMS works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity, Google or Keycloak. To set it up, see [Configure single sign-on](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/configure_single_sign_on/index.md).

Login page with single sign-on

## Password and single sign-on

|                     | Password                               | Single sign-on                                                                    |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Credentials kept by | Ella IMS                               | The identity provider, with its own policies, such as multi-factor authentication |
| Role set by         | An Admin                               | An Admin, or the user's groups at the identity provider                           |
| Session             | 30 days                                | The session lifetime, 24 hours by default                                         |
| Access removed by   | Deleting the user in Ella IMS, at once | Removing the user at the identity provider, at the end of their session           |

Password login stays when single sign-on is on, and at least one Admin always keeps a password. An identity provider that is down or misconfigured cannot lock everyone out.

## Matching users

A user is matched to their account at the identity provider, not to their email address, so a changed or reused email address does not give access to another user. The email address is used once, to link the account at its first login, and only if the identity provider has verified it. A provider that does not say whether email addresses are verified, such as Microsoft Entra ID, must be trusted explicitly: anyone who can set their email address there could take over the matching user. An account with no user in Ella IMS gets one only from a [group mapping](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#map-groups-to-roles).

## Offboarding

Ella IMS does not learn when someone is removed at the identity provider. Their session lasts until its lifetime ends, and their API tokens until deleted. A shorter session lifetime narrows that window, at the cost of logging in more often. To end access at once, [offboard the user](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/manage_single_sign_on_users/#offboard-a-user) in Ella IMS.

## Client secret

The identity provider's client secret is stored in the database, `db.path` in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/reference/config_file/index.md), and so in any copy of it.

# SIP Trunks

A SIP trunk connects Ella IMS to a carrier, for calls to and from numbers outside the HSS.

SIP trunks

## The border

- **BGCF**: picks the trunk for a call out.
- **IBCF**: the border with carriers. It hides the IMS from them.
- **TrGW**: relays the voice.

## Calls out

1. A phone calls a number that the HSS doesn't know.
1. Ella IMS takes the route with the longest matching prefix, else the default route.
1. It tries the route's trunks in order, skipping those that are down or disabled.

Short codes never go to a trunk.

## Calls in

Ella IMS finds the trunk by the call's source address, and routes the call to the subscriber with the called number.

## Trust

Ella IMS accepts the caller's number only from a trusted trunk. Mark a trunk trusted only if you have an interconnect agreement with the carrier.

## Voice

Ella IMS relays the voice without transcoding, so phones and the carrier must share a codec, such as AMR-WB. A carrier that accepts only G.711 needs a transcoding SBC.

## Keepalives

Ella IMS sends OPTIONS requests to each trunk. A trunk that stops answering is down until it answers again.

## Not supported

- Emergency calls
- Video, fax and messages
- Registration with the carrier
- SRTP

# SMS over IP

Ella IMS includes an IP Short Message Gateway (IP-SM-GW), which lets phones send and receive SMS over IMS.

SMS over IP

## Sending

1. The phone sends the SMS as a SIP MESSAGE, which reaches the IP-SM-GW through the P-CSCF and the S-CSCF.
1. The IP-SM-GW forwards it to the SMSC of the SMS route of the phone's service centre address, or of the default route if no route has that address.

## Receiving

1. While the phone registers with SMS over IP, the IP-SM-GW registers at the HSS for the subscriber.
1. The HSS then sends the SMSC's routing requests for the subscriber to the IP-SM-GW.
1. The IP-SM-GW delivers over IMS first, then over NAS through the MME or SMSF.

## SMS routes

An SMS route maps a service centre address to the SMS-IWMSC that serves it, usually part of the SMSC. TS 29.338 leaves this mapping to local configuration. A route names the SMS-IWMSC by its Diameter host, so its peers need one.

The default route works the same way, for every service centre address no other route has. It cannot hand short messages to a Diameter routing agent to route by realm, another fallback TS 29.338 allows: an SMS-IWMSC behind such an agent needs its own peer.

Routes are separate from peers. A peer is a Diameter connection, shared by every application it serves. A route is a choice of the IP-SM-GW alone. An SMSC's connection appears with the other peers on the **Cores** page; its routes appear on the **SMS over IP** page.
